# What Loom can draw (generated by `py -m loom catalog`; do not hand-edit)

One line each on WHEN to use it. Details: `get_api_section(<section>)`; templates and blueprints: the catalogue.

## assets

- **vendor_art** (runtime/art.js; section: Vendor art): a licence-checked illustration (a plant, a cup, a food) when no kit object fits; literal set:name references only. Call: `Loom.art.place(ctx, name, "set:name", {x, y, size, colors, t})`

## clips

- **clip_manim** (runtime/manim/loom_manim.py; section: loom-scene-author: Manim scenes): exact mathematics, plots, equations, geometry that moves precisely (Manim, rendered to a transparent clip). Call: `storyboard kind "manim"; scenes/<beat>.py (a LoomScene), or a manim blueprint with params`
- **clip_skia** (runtime/skia/loom_skia.py; section: TOOLBOX: skia): a painterly or glowing hero image with blur, gradients and light (Skia, a transparent clip). Call: `storyboard kind "skia"; scenes/<beat>_skia.py`
- **clip_three** (runtime/three/render.mjs; section: TOOLBOX: three): a real 3D object or device turning, opening or changing state, or an isometric diorama (Three.js, a transparent clip); start from the model library (models3d). Call: `storyboard kind "three"; scenes/<beat>_three.js`
- **models3d** (assets/models3d; section: TOOLBOX: three): a ready 3D object with keys you drive from time (a phone with a screen, a padlock that opens, a rack that alerts); load the three tool for the details. Call: `in a kind "three" clip: await X.model(id, opts); m.set(key, value)`
  - `accelerator_chip`: one generic accelerator package close up: a board, a package substrate, a large central die with a grid of cores, memory stacks beside the die on the same substrate, and a liquid cold plate with an inlet and an outlet hose that lowers onto it
  - `agent_sandbox`: an AI agent's sandbox: a glass room on a plinth with a softly lit core on a pedestal (a stand-in for the agent, no robot), a back wall of labelled tool sockets of which only the allowed ones get plugged in, and a gate at the front with a status light that a human approves
  - `badge_door`: a security door in a metal frame set in a wall, a badge reader beside it with a status light, and a marked one-person zone on the floor; opts.pair builds a two-door mantrap (a glass vestibule) whose second door cannot open while the first is open
  - `balance_scale`: a two-pan beam balance (a lab balance, not a courtroom symbol): a base and pillar, a beam with a pointer over a tick arc, two pans hanging level on strings; labelled blocks drop into the pans and the beam settles to the side the caller states
  - `bar_chart`: a 3D bar chart on a plinth: rounded bars that grow to their values, one highlighted, labels on the plinth's front
  - `bicycle`: a road bicycle at real proportions (metres): a diamond frame of tubes (top, down and seat tubes, chain and seat stays), a raked fork, two 700c wheels with rims, tyres, hubs and 32 spokes each, a drivetrain (chainring with teeth, cranks, pedals, a rear cassette and the chain), a saddle on its post, a stem and a flat bar
  - `building`: an office tower: glass bands of windows that light floor by floor, a canopy over the entrance, a roof plant
  - `cdu`: a generic coolant distribution unit: a floor-standing cabinet whose door (with a control display) opens on a reservoir, two pumps, a filter, valves and a plate heat exchanger; two separate loops, the facility (primary) loop on the right and the technology (secondary) loop to the racks on the left, meet only across the exchanger plates; four pipe ends on top
  - `chunk_cabinet`: an index cabinet of shallow drawers, each a document chunk with a short label (from opts); pages drop in and become drawers, a query card arrives and a beam sweeps, the caller's top-k drawers slide out in rank order and their cards lift into a stack (into the prompt)
  - `ci_conveyor`: a delivery pipeline as a conveyor: changes ride the belt as labelled crates through a row of labelled stations, each with a status lamp and a gate that lifts when its check passes; a failing crate is pushed off onto a return chute while the line keeps running
  - `clock`: a round desk clock on two feet: a rim, a face with hour marks (no numbers), hour and minute hands, a red seconds hand
  - `cloud`: a soft, puffy 3D cloud with an arrow that moves up or down through it (sync, upload, download)
  - `coin_stack`: stacks of milled coins that build up coin by coin (or drain away), up to three stacks
  - `credit_card`: a payment card with no brand: a chip, a contactless mark, grouped number dots (or the digits given), a magnetic stripe on the back
  - `dc_aisle_pair`: a hot and cold aisle pair: two rows of server racks (the library's server_rack) whose fronts face each other across a cold aisle, with a hot aisle behind each row, cooling units at the row ends, ladder cable trays on the rack tops, and supply from a raised floor with perforated tiles in the cold aisle only, from an overhead duct, or from a fan wall; cold or hot aisle containment
  - `dc_hall`: a data hall for an establishing shot or a fly-through: pairs of rack rows whose fronts face each other across cold aisles (perforated tiles in the cold aisles only on a raised floor), hot aisles behind, ladder cable trays and power busway over every row hung from a ceiling grid, linear lights over the cold aisles, perimeter cooling units on the end wall lined up with the hot aisles, and coolant distribution units on the back wall; walls cut away on the near sides
  - `dc_security_layers`: an isometric cutaway of a data centre's physical security layers, outside in: a perimeter fence with a sliding gate and reader, the building shell with a badge door into the lobby, a mantrap (the library's badge_door pair) into the secure corridor, the data hall with its own badge door, a mesh cage inside the hall, and a locked rack (server_rack) in the cage; every checkpoint has a reader whose light stays on once access is logged
  - `desk_set`: a workstation: a desk with a monitor (the monitor model), a keyboard, a mug, a plant and an office chair tucked in
  - `document`: a printed document standing on its edge, a stack behind it; a stamp lands on it
  - `earth`: the Earth as a sphere with its real coastlines (Natural Earth 1:110m, given in the context or opts.rings), a graticule every 30 degrees, an atmosphere shell, pins at given places (each its own part, pin0, pin1, ...) and great-circle arcs between them that draw on
  - `electric_motorbike`: a generic electric motorcycle at real proportions (metres): an aluminium twin-spar frame around a large battery pack whose side cover lifts to show its cell modules (cylindrical cells with busbars), a finned controller under the seat with orange high-voltage cables to a mid-mounted motor (housing, stator teeth wound with copper coils, a rotor with magnets), a toothed belt from the motor pulley to the rear wheel, a swingarm with a coil-over shock, an upside-down fork with triple clamps, 17 inch cast wheels with real tyre sections, twin front and one rear brake disc with calipers, a seat, bars with mirrors, a headlight, a tank cover and a tail
  - `embedding_space`: an embedding space: a faint box with three unlabelled axes holding a point cloud that settles into clusters (words beside them from opts), a query point whose k nearest neighbours light and link, and two analogy arrows between real points
  - `envelope`: a paper envelope standing up, back towards us: the flap opens and a letter rises out; with opts.attachment a paper clip holds a file tag to the letter
  - `folder`: a card file folder standing up: a back with a tab, papers inside, a front flap that opens; a label on the tab
  - `gear`: a pair of meshing machined gears on a base plate: a large drive gear and a small one, turning together
  - `generator_set`: a generic containerised standby generator for outdoors (or its own room): an enclosure with louvres and service doors on a fuel tank base and skid, a radiator grille with its fan at one end, a control panel and a status beacon at the other, a roof silencer and exhaust stack with a rain cap, and an output conduit
  - `globe`: a desk globe on a meridian ring and stand: a sphere with a graticule of latitude and longitude, pins that rise at given places
  - `gpu_server`: a generic 8-accelerator AI server lying flat with its lid removable: a front fan wall, eight identical accelerator modules in two rows of four on one baseboard linked all-to-all through a row of switch chips, a CPU board with two sockets and memory on a shelf at the rear, power supplies and a network card bay; air-cooled (tall finned heatsinks, many fans) or liquid-cooled (flat cold plates on supply and return manifolds, fewer fans, a shorter chassis)
  - `holo_building`: a generic ten-storey office building over a double-height lobby, built as a hologram hero (T-146): a concrete core with its lift overrun, ten floor slabs (floor1 at the bottom to floor10 at the top, each a named part inside floors), perimeter columns, a curtain-wall facade on the two long sides (mullions on a 4 m module, a spandrel band at every floor) and solid end walls with a glazed stair strip, a colonnade lobby with an entrance canopy and a revolving-door drum, and the roof plant (parapet, a louvred plant screen, two cooling towers, two air-handling units and ducts); the glass stays see-through, so the floors and the core read inside it
  - `holo_gpu`: a generic dual-slot, triple-fan graphics card built as a hologram hero (T-138), standing on its edge connector: a shroud with three fan openings, three fans of eleven swept blades, a heatsink of three fin stacks with heat pipes bending over its top edge, the board (gold edge fingers with their key notch, the GPU package, eight memory chips, a row of power stages), two 8-pin power connectors on its top edge, the I/O bracket with four display outputs (three of one socket shape, one of a wider shape) and vent slots, and a backplate; every part a real, connected piece that explodes along the card's thickness
  - `holo_laptop`: a generic 14-inch class laptop built as a hologram hero (T-137): a bottom case on rubber feet with rear exhaust slots and screws, a keyboard deck with its speaker slots, a full key layout (function row, five rows on a 15-unit grid, an inverted-T arrow cluster), a glass trackpad, a hinge barrel, a lid with its display, bezel and camera, and an I/O module of ports on the left side; every part a real, connected piece that explodes along its own axis
  - `id_badge`: a staff ID badge on a lanyard clip: a card with a header band, a portrait silhouette, a name and a role
  - `key`: a classic door key: a round bow with a hole, a shank and a cut bit, in brushed metal
  - `laptop`: an open laptop: aluminium base with a keyboard and trackpad, a hinged lid with a live screen
  - `lightbulb`: a classic glass light bulb on a ridged screw base; its filament glows and a halo blooms when it turns on
  - `loss_landscape`: a loss surface over two weights on a plinth: a smooth lit surface (low is cool, high is warm) with its contour map on the floor, a ball that descends by gradient descent computed from the surface's own slope, and a trail of its steps
  - `meeting_room`: a small meeting room diorama (two walls cut away): a table with six chairs and no people, a wall screen, a whiteboard, a wall clock on a shelf, a door
  - `monitor`: a desktop monitor on a stand: thin bezel, live screen, a round foot
  - `neural_lattice`: a toy neural network: three to five layers of nodes (each layer a faint glass pane on a base) with every node linked to every node of the next layer; link thickness is the weight; a pulse runs forward and nodes light by their computed activation, a second pulse runs back and links change (learning), or only a marked few change (fine-tuning)
  - `office_floor`: an open-plan office floor: pods of desks back to back (each the library's desk_set: desk, monitor, chair, mug and plant) with low dividers, tall plants, and a glass meeting pod with a round table; no people
  - `padlock`: a padlock: a solid rounded body with a keyhole and a steel shackle that springs open
  - `phone`: a smartphone standing upright: glossy shell, glass face with a live screen, camera bump, side keys
  - `power_path`: an isometric 2N power chain: two separate paths, A and B, each from its own utility feed through a transformer and switchgear with a transfer switch (its own standby generator wired to that switch), a UPS (the library's ups_cabinet) and an output breaker to its own rack power strip (rack_pdu), ending at one dual-supply server whose two power supplies take one cord from each path; the generators (generator_set) stand outside the lanes
  - `rack_pdu`: a vertical zero-U rack power strip: a tall housing in its feed's colour, a column of equipment outlets in groups with a light by each, breakers, a small load meter, a feed tag and an input cord with an industrial plug; optionally the A and B pair side by side
  - `security_key`: a hardware security key: a small rounded fob with a metal connector, a key ring hole and a touch pad that glows
  - `server_rack`: a server cabinet (v2): a frame holding a column of servers, each with vents and a status light, a top-of-rack switch, a perforated front door, blanking panels for empty units, two vertical power strips A and B and cable bundles at the open rear; air runs front to back
  - `shield`: a solid heraldic shield with a raised rim and an embossed mark (tick, cross or none)
  - `shredder`: an office shredder: a bin on casters with a window, a cutting head with a feed slot and a status light; a document feeds into the slot and the shreds fill the bin
  - `tablet`: a tablet in a slim case standing on its long edge (opts.portrait stands it upright): glass face with a live screen, a case lip round the glass, a camera in the case's corner cut-out
  - `tor_switch`: a generic 1U top-of-rack network switch: two rows of port cages with link lights and a block of larger uplink cages on the port face; two power supplies and a row of fan modules on the other face; rack ears
  - `transformer_stack`: a decoder-only transformer as a tower of identical blocks (each an attention slab and a feed-forward slab) on an embedding base, with a residual rail up its side; token tiles rise block by block, one block opens to show its causal attention pattern, and a row of probability bars grows on top with the highest lit
  - `ups_cabinet`: a generic UPS row cabinet: a power bay with a display and a power-flow mimic, and a battery bay whose door opens on shelves of battery blocks; an input cable and an output cable on top
- **three_presets** (runtime/three/presets; section: TOOLBOX: three): a ready 3D shot whose content is params: device_shot shows a phone, tablet, laptop, monitor or desk with its screen and moments on spoken words, and the device stays swappable after the storyboard. Call: `storyboard kind "three" with three.preset (params only, nothing to write); py -m loom device <id> <beat> <device> swaps a device beat later`
  - `device_shot`: one device from the model library, its screen and its moments driven by spoken words; the device, screen and mood are params, so the engine can swap them after the storyboard
  - `holo_hero`: a hologram hero (hologram v2): one library model shown as projected light on a projector pad (Fresnel rims, its real edges, scan bands, a scan plane that builds it, a hot part, depth fog, bloom and a slight fringe), turning on a turntable, its parts exploding on the word; it exports its parts' screen boxes so the hologram HUD's locks and datums point at them
  - `model_shot`: one library model or set (assets/models3d) on a lit stage, its keys driven by spoken words; the model, its options, its states and the mood are params, so nothing is written and everything stays swappable

## data

- **data_pictures** (runtime/data.js; section: Data as a picture): a number drawn as a picture (a counter that runs, as many things as the quantity, a line that dips at the event), never a number on a card. Call: `Loom.data.counter, unitGrid, barsOn, dipLine, profile, tag, chapter, stamp, pile, flood; Loom.array`
- **geography** (runtime/geo.js; section: Real geography): a true map or globe: countries flood, cities mark, arcs travel (where in the world it happens). Call: `Loom.geo.map, Loom.geo.globe, Loom.geo.city`

## drawing

- **brush** (runtime/brush.js; section: Real-media marks): pencil, charcoal, marker and ink lines, watercolour washes and hatching that look hand-made (p5.brush), painted once and revealed in drawing order; for hand-drawn, whiteboard and paper styles. Call: `Loom.brush.paint(ctx, name, {x, y, w, h, layers: [{at, reveal, draw: (b, W, H) => ...}]})`
- **brush_recipes** (runtime/recipes_brush.js; section: Real-media marks): ready hand-made marks: pencil rings round the red flags of a real email in spoken order, a reviewer's circles, brackets and strikes over a diff or a draft, a system sketched box by box as it is named, a watercolour wash behind one phrase. Call: `Loom.brush.redFlags, markup, sketchSystem, wash (ctx, name, opts)`

## essentials

- **treatments** (runtime/treat.js; section: Treatments): labels, speech or thought bubbles, panels, badges and ticks drawn in the lesson's own seeded form. Call: `Loom.treat.label, bubble, panel, badge, mark`

## frames

- **templates** (runtime/catalog.json; section: catalog): a frame-layout beat (a definition, a list, a comparison, a quiz) laid out in the whole frame; one id at most max(2, 15 % of beats) times. Call: `storyboard kind "template"`
  - `calendar.plan`: A schedule the learner will copy into their own calendar.
  - `chart.bars`: Compare quantities.
  - `compare.two`: Two sides as equals (before/after, do/don't, myth/fact, A vs B).
  - `cycle`: A loop that returns (3-6 stages).
  - `definition`: Define one term.
  - `document.page`: A page the learner recognises (notes, an email, a policy excerpt, a form).
  - `icon.grid`: A set of PEERS (3-6 members of one category).
  - `list.steps`: An ordered procedure or checklist (3-6 items).
  - `process.flow`: A process that runs (3-5 steps).
  - `quiz.answer`: A stopping check, part 2 of 2.
  - `quiz.question`: A stopping check, part 1 of 2.
  - `quote`: A line worth hearing exactly: the quote mark drops, the words print (unmask), attribution settles last.
  - `recap`: Consolidate: 3-5 tokens (icon + short label) light up one by one ON their words, joined by a thread that draws through them.
  - `scenario.dialogue`: Two characters in a moment (manager/employee, customer/agent...).
  - `stat.hero`: ONE number that matters.
  - `timeline`: Events in time.
  - `title.card`: Opener, section divider or payoff title.
- **blueprints** (runtime/catalog.json; section: catalog): a ready-made motion piece (a meter, a character moment, a journey, a hub, a portal). Call: `storyboard kind "blueprint"`
  - `hero.character_moment`: One character in a moment, with a thought or memory bubble whose contents CHANGE over time (ideas arriving, fading, being recalled).
  - `hero.hub`: A system with a centre and satellites (a GDS and airlines, a manager and a team, a brain and its cues).
  - `hero.journey`: A traveller moves along a path through waypoints (days, stages, attempts) ON their words.
  - `hero.meter`: An instrument whose reading changes over time (memory strength, risk, progress, confidence).
  - `hero.portal`: Draws a frame (screen, lens or card) that the NEXT station is nested inside, so a 'zoom' join flies the camera through it - an infinite-canvas move that reads as going deeper.

## fx

- **fx_moments** (runtime/fx.js; section: Expressive motion): a light sweep across a payoff, or a spotlight that dims everything but one region; the pack's grain, vignette and paper. Call: `ctx.fxMoment("light" or "spotlight", t0, t1, rect); storyboard scene fx`

## joins

- **material_joins** (runtime/material.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): a join made of the frame's material (paper tears, a page turns, a shape fills); one material per lesson. Call: `storyboard join_in.type torn, page, scroll, motif, handoff, fill`

## kit

- **kit_primitives** (runtime/kit.js; section: kit): the measured drawing primitives every element uses (text fitted to real font metrics, shapes, ticks, icons, peep busts). Call: `kit.text, fit, rect, card, pill, disc, line, path, arrow, mark, icon, peep; row, col, split`

## layout

- **layout_guard** (runtime/layout.js; section: Layout): the engine moves labels, tags and edge-crossing texts clear of collisions and the frame edge, deterministically (D-169). Call: `Loom.layout.solve, plan offsets in kit.element and treat.label`

## library

- **components** (runtime/components.js; section: ctx): a small library element (a card, a chip) reused instead of redrawn; see catalog_search(query, "component"). Call: `ctx.use(id, params, {x, y, name})`
- **component_list** (runtime/catalog.json; section: ctx): promoted small elements. Call: `ctx.use(id, params)`
  - `ai_context_window`: A context window as a budget: one bar for the model's limit, filled with labelled segments (system prompt, instructions, history, retrieved documents, the answer's reserve) with their token counts, the total against the limit, an overflow drawn past the end, and the oldest tokens sliding out at the left when the history is truncated.
  - `ai_guardrails`: An AI guardrail pipeline: the user's input, input checks (personal data, prompt injection, topic policy) as gates, the model, output checks (toxicity, grounding, personal data) as gates, and the response; each gate passes, flags or blocks, a blocked request turns back with its reason, and a token runs the pipeline gate by gate.
  - `ai_llm_console`: An LLM console: role-labelled blocks for the system prompt, the user, the assistant and tools, prompts in mono and answers in the body face, tool calls with their arguments and result, the assistant's answer streaming in, a footer with tokens in and out and the stop reason, and spans that can be redacted.
  - `ai_token_distribution`: Next-token probabilities: the context so far, the candidate next tokens as bars with their percentages, a temperature dial that sharpens or flattens them, a top-p cut that greys out the tail, and the sampled token marked and appended to the context.
  - `app_analytics`: An analytics workspace: a dashboard's filters, headline numbers, a grid of charts and a table under them, walked through by a pointer that changes a filter so every number answers, drills into one bar so the table narrows to it, and exports the view.
  - `app_calendar`: A calendar at work in week view: days across, hours down, events placed by their times, the guests' free and busy times in a booking form, walked through by a pointer that creates an event, drags one to reschedule it, opens one and invites a colleague.
  - `app_chat_workspace`: A team chat workspace: channels and direct messages, a channel's conversation with mentions, reactions, file cards and threads, and a composer, walked through by a pointer that opens a channel, posts, reacts and opens a thread.
  - `app_cloud_console`: A cloud provider's console: services in a sidebar, the project and region, a list of resources with their status, and one resource's detail with its settings, metrics, access roles and logs, walked through by a pointer that creates a resource, scales it, attaches a role and reads its logs.
  - `app_docs_editor`: A shared document editor: a page of headings, paragraphs and lists, suggested edits shown inline, comments in the margin, and a version history, walked through by a pointer that types, comments on a phrase, accepts a suggestion and restores an earlier version.
  - `app_email`: An email client at work: folders, a thread list with unread and flagged mail, the open message in a reading pane, and a compose window, walked through by a pointer that opens, replies, flags, moves and searches.
  - `app_hris`: An HR system an employee and a manager use: the employee's profile with leave balances, a time off request form with past requests, the team's org chart and a manager's approvals queue, walked through by a pointer that requests leave, approves or declines a request and views the team.
  - `app_ide_workspace`: A developer's workspace: a file tree, editor tabs, code with syntax colour and line numbers, a terminal and a problems list, a source control panel and a debug toolbar, walked through by a pointer that opens a file, runs a command, steps through code in the debugger and commits a change.
  - `app_lms_course`: An online course on a learning platform: the outline of modules and lessons with what is done, a lesson player, a quiz with feedback, the learner's progress and a certificate, walked through by a pointer that starts a lesson, answers, submits and completes the course.
  - `app_project_board`: A project tracker a team works in: a board of columns with work-in-progress limits and issue cards, a backlog list, and an issue's detail with its assignee and sub-tasks, walked through by a pointer that creates an issue, drags a card to another column, assigns it and closes it.
  - `dev_ci_pipeline`: A CI/CD pipeline: stages as cards joined by arrows, each with its jobs, a status icon per job and stage (passed, failed, running, pending, skipped, blocked) and durations; on cue the stages run in order, jobs spin and resolve, and a failed stage stops the flow so the stages after it are skipped.
  - `dev_code_editor`: A code editor pane: a tab with the file name and its language, line numbers in a gutter, code in syntax colour, an overview stripe and an optional status line; lines type in on cue, a range can be brought into focus, a span marked with a squiggle and a line replaced.
  - `dev_db_table`: A database table: an optional SQL query bar, column headers with their types, rows of cells with numbers right aligned, the rows past the limit summed up in one line and a row count; on cue the query types and its rows arrive, a filter collapses the rows that do not match, a cell is marked and a column of personal data is masked.
  - `dev_diff_view`: A code diff: the file's changed hunks with old and new line numbers, removed lines on a faint failure band with a minus, added lines on a faint success band with a plus and context lines plain, unified or side by side; removals then additions reveal on cue and a review comment can open on a row.
  - `dev_git_graph`: A branch and commit graph: one lane per branch with its name at the left, commits as dots in the order they were made, lines from each commit to its parents (curves where branches fork and merge), tags as small flags and a ring for where HEAD points; commits pop in on cue, a merge draws itself and HEAD travels.
  - `dev_http_exchange`: An HTTP exchange: a request card with its method, URL, headers and body, and a response card with its status code and reason, headers and body, joined by an arrow with an optional latency; secret header values are masked until revealed, and on cue the request travels and the response arrives.
  - `dev_terminal`: A terminal session: a window with a title bar, commands typed after a prompt on cue and their output printed under them, errors and successes in their own tones, a block cursor, and lines that scroll when the window is full.
  - `ops_alert_card`: An alert or page notification card: a severity badge, the alert's title, the service and the time it fired, and its state (firing, acknowledged, resolved) by icon and edge bar; it can sit on a pile of earlier alerts, be acknowledged, resolved, or escalated with a second card sliding in under it.
  - `ops_cloud_architecture`: A cloud architecture: nested frames for the cloud, its regions, availability zones, networks and public or private subnets, generic service nodes inside them, and links between the nodes; the frames reveal from the outside in, a zone fails and its nodes go dark, a request flows along a path.
  - `ops_cluster_map`: A container cluster: nodes as panels with their name and resource use, pods as small tiles inside them named by service and marked by state (running, pending, failed, terminating), and an optional control plane; pods are scheduled onto nodes, a node fails and its pods are rescheduled, a service scales up or down.
  - `ops_incident_timeline`: An incident timeline: a time axis with the incident's phases as bands, events as pins with their time, kind and label set in rows so they never collide, long quiet gaps drawn as a break in the axis, and brackets for durations such as time to detect and time to resolve; the events reveal in time order.
  - `ops_metric_tile`: A monitoring metric tile: the metric's name, its current value large with its unit, a sparkline of recent values with warning and critical threshold lines, and a state (ok, warning, critical) shown by tone, icon and edge bar; new points push in and the value counts.
  - `ops_rollout`: A deployment rollout: traffic as a stream of dots from a router to instances of the old and the new version, the split as a percentage, instances that switch over step by step (rolling), all at once (blue-green) or as a growing share (canary), an instance that turns unhealthy, and a rollback.
  - `ops_slo_budget`: An SLO and its error budget: the target as a big figure over its window, a bar of the budget left that burns down as errors spend it, the budget left in time units and the share used, a burn-rate arrow, and a freeze state when the budget is spent.

## media

- **footage** (runtime/footage.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): consented real video graded in tokens, frozen and annotated (needs consent; downloads need approval). Call: `Loom.footage(ctx, name, {src, trim, at, grade})`
- **lottie** (runtime/lottie.js; section: Expressive motion): a designer-made Lottie animation as an element, seeked by the timeline, recoloured to tokens. Call: `ctx.lottie(name, id, {at, speed, loop, colors})`

## motion

- **springs_and_gestures** (runtime/expressive.js; section: Expressive motion): arrivals with life (springs, orchestrated groups) and gestures that say wrong, look here, tapped, done; sound events. Call: `Loom.spring, m.spring, m.group, m.groupExit, m.shake, m.nudge, m.press, m.glow, Loom.sfx`
- **hold_and_transform** (runtime/hold.js; section: Hold and transform): keep the shot and change it (a lid lifts off, a colour heats, layers peel past the camera) instead of cutting. Call: `Loom.hold.lift, heat, peel, breathe`
- **motion_vocabulary** (runtime/motion.js; section: motion): the motion vocabulary every reveal uses, timed on the spoken word. Call: `m.reveal, settle, pop, stamp, drop, converge, grow, draw, unmask, iris, count, along, travel, highlight, emphasis, exit`
- **orb** (runtime/orbs.js; section: AI thinking orb): a dotted orb that shows an AI assistant working, searching, solving, listening or composing (thinking-orbs), and Loom's unsure, checking and paused states, frame-exact; only where the lesson shows an AI tool at work. Call: `Loom.orb(ctx, name, {x, y, size, state, t, until, tint, states})`
- **physics** (runtime/physics.js; section: Real physics, baked): things that fall, pile up, collide, topple or roll (a backlog piling into a bin, a stack that topples, a chain reaction), simulated once with Matter.js and replayed frame-exactly. Call: `Loom.physics.world(ctx, name, {...}).body(...).run()`
- **orb_recipes** (runtime/recipes_orb.js; section: AI thinking orb): ready AI-assistant moments: an agent's plan, act, observe loop with its tool cards, an answer retrieved from documents with a citation, a fluent answer checked and found unsure, a draft paused for a person's approval. Call: `Loom.orb.toolLoop, retrieval, unsure, approval (ctx, name, opts)`
- **physics_recipes** (runtime/recipes_physics.js; section: Real physics, baked): ready physics teaching moments: layered defences that each stop some, items sorted into named bins, a fixed context window overflowing, a reply-all flood, a locked test split, a weighted next-token draw, a biased funnel, priorities in a jar, a spare support, energy split into IT and overhead. Call: `Loom.physics.sieve, sortIntoBins, contextWindow, inboxFlood, trainTestSplit, nextTokenDraw, biasedFunnel, priorityJar, redundancyTopple, puePour (ctx, name, opts)`

## people

- **hands** (runtime/hands.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): hands as presenters (pointing at a diagram, carrying an object in); designed art only, a placeholder set today. Call: `Loom.hands.enter, pose, point, place, exit`
- **presenter_and_captions** (runtime/overlay.js; section: Layering and joins): the code-drawn presenter beside a title, or with a card of up to 3 short lines; burnt-in captions. Call: `storyboard kind avatar (props title, kicker, card); captions`
- **character_rigs** (runtime/rig.js; section: Characters): a person who acts (poses, gestures, lip flaps, a walk) from a designed rig; story.cast fixes each person's look. Call: `ctx.character(name, rigId, {x, y, scale, pose, emotion})`
- **avatar** (runtime/overlay.js; section: Layering and joins): A code-drawn presenter in a disc beside a kicker and title; with `card`, up to three short lines (or one rule) fill the empty side and the disc steps back.. Call: `storyboard kind "avatar"`
  - `props`: card, cast, cloth, frame_fill, frame_r, kicker, member, name, role_label, say_title, side, talk_emotion, title, title_cue
- **rig_ids** (runtime/rigs, assets/rigs; section: Characters): the designed rigs a person can be drawn with (peep members for templates: woman, man, girl, boy, elder_woman, elder_man). Call: `ctx.character(name, rigId, ...); story.cast {name, rig or member, skin, cloth}`
  - `ava`
  - `extra`
  - `maya`
  - `pip`
  - `sam`
  - `tess`

## primitive

- **magnifier_and_cutaway** (runtime/magnify.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): point at a detail without cutting away (a lens with a leader line), or open a window into an object. Call: `Loom.magnify(ctx, name, {source, focus, zoom, t}), Loom.magnify.cutaway`
- **morph** (runtime/morph.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): one drawn shape becomes another (a cell becomes a coin), or grows to become the next field. Call: `Loom.morph.to, chain, shape, fill; m.morph`
- **swap_slot** (runtime/slot.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): hold the layout and change its contents on the spoken word (swap, flip, slide, recolour, relabel, stamp). Call: `Loom.slot(ctx, name, {x, y, w, h}).show, sequence`
- **stepped_time** (runtime/stepped.js; section: Primitives from the TED-Ed study): hand-made timing (drawings on twos or threes) and a boiling outline; illustrated packs only. Call: `Loom.stepped.on, wrap, ease, boil`

## style

- **style_engine** (runtime/engines.js; section: The style's engine): call the working code that solves the style's hard part (runtime/engines/<style>.js); whiteboard, blueprint, isometric, hologram and screencast exist (D-179, D-183, D-185). Call: `ctx.engine; Loom.engines.define`
- **template_skins** (runtime/skins.js; section: The style's engine): a style draws the catalog templates its own way (the hand, the nib, light, the board, the product); templates are unchanged. Call: `Loom.skins.define (in an engine file)`

## timing

- **timing_grid** (runtime/grid.js; section: The timing grid): land a motion on the lesson's shared clock: a named hit, a bar line or a music beat the mix also uses (D-173). Call: `ctx.hit, ctx.bar, ctx.onBeat; Loom.grid`

## tool

- **trailer** (runtime/trailer.js; section: Look at the film): a 20 to 35 s course trailer cut from an approved lesson (a cut of the film, not a scene builder). Call: `py -m loom trailer <id>`

## ui

- **product_in_use** (runtime/interaction.js; section: Expressive motion): show a product in use: a cursor moves on an arc, taps a button, types into a field. Call: `ui.window, field, button, toast, cursor; m.tap, m.typeInto`
- **ui_artefacts** (runtime/ui_artefacts.js; section: UI artefacts): the real thing a workplace lesson is about (an email, an inbox, a chat, a page), every word real. Call: `Loom.ui.mail, inbox, chat, doc; ui.build, mark, card, wire`

## world

- **depth_25d** (runtime/depth.js; section: Depth stage): a 2.5D landscape or room in parallax layers with depth of field (cinematic packs); keep text out of the stage. Call: `ctx.depth(name, {dolly, push, drift, focus, dof, atmosphere})`
- **glow_kit** (runtime/glow.js; section: Glow kit): a procedural saturated world that is alive and full without drawn assets (the glow-flat register; works in any pack). Call: `Loom.glow.ground, shafts, blob, burst, vortex, orbit, swarm, hud, compare, gauge`
- **isometric** (runtime/iso.js; section: Isometric): an isometric diagram of a system, a building or a flow (boxes extrude on their words). Call: `ctx.iso({x0, y0, unit}): box, tile, grid, arrow, label, done`
- **objects** (runtime/objects.js; section: Objects): a thing the narration names drawn as a thing (document, envelope, calendar, clock, phone, laptop, folder, package, building, heart, bulb, lock) with states. Call: `Loom.obj.draw(ctx, name, kind, {state, t}), Loom.obj.shape`
- **places_and_camera** (runtime/places.js; section: Places and the camera): a motion beat that happens somewhere (an office, a server room), explored with an in-scene camera. Call: `Loom.place.office, inside, server, meeting, warehouse; Loom.cam.push, pan, pull, frame`
- **scenery_sets** (runtime/scenery.js; section: Scenery): a set that fills the frame, grey extras for a crowd, a black narration card for a turn in the story. Call: `ctx.scenery("room" or "stage" or "street", name, o), ctx.crowd, ctx.narrationCard`
- **set_library** (runtime/sets.js; section: Drawn sets from the library): a beat that happens in a designed place from the set library (office/meeting_room ...), with characters at its anchors and content in its screen slot. Call: `Loom.place.set(ctx, name, id?) with R.anchors, R.slot(name), R.relight(setup, t0, dur) and the place camera`
- **world_and_joins** (runtime/world.js; section: Screen joins): one canvas for the film: stations, camera joins and zoom-throughs, held elements, motifs that travel between stations. Call: `storyboard stations, join_in (camera, travel, zoom, cut, iris, wipe, dip, fade), keep, ctx.held, ctx.motif`
- **world_packs** (packs/worlds; section: Places and the camera): pick the world a lesson happens in; its places, people and props are already designed or listed to commission. Call: `a world's scenes, cast and assets (docs/assets/WORLD_PACKS.md)`
  - `city`: City and public spaces: the commute and travel to work, safety on foot and in public, working in public places, arriving at the office, accessibility in public, customer journeys
  - `classroom`: Classroom and training: teaching and facilitation, learner support and safeguarding, presenting to an audience, study skills and information literacy, further and higher education
  - `construction`: Construction site: working at height, permits to work, site induction, toolbox talks, excavations and buried services, site traffic, PPE
  - `contact_centre`: Contact centre and customer service: call handling, complaints, empathy, de-escalation, vulnerable customers, identity checks and data protection, quality coaching, team huddles, wellbeing after difficult calls
  - `factory`: Factory and manufacturing: machine safety, lockout tagout, quality and defects, near-miss reporting, PPE, process alarms, lean and continuous improvement
  - `finance`: Bank and finance: anti-money laundering and know your customer checks, fraud and scams, conduct and market abuse, mis-selling and suitability, customer vulnerability, dual control and secure access, data protection
  - `healthcare`: Healthcare and clinic: patient safety, infection control, medicines, consent, confidentiality, handovers, de-escalation, wellbeing of staff
  - `history`: History and period worlds: how work used to be: the origins of safety law, pay and record keeping, fair trading and consumer protection, office work before computers, change over time
  - `home`: Home and remote work: hybrid and remote work, wellbeing and switching off, security and scams at home, ergonomics at home, family life
  - `metaphor`: Metaphor worlds: abstract ideas made concrete through one real place: hidden risk, safe passage and trust, building toward each other, systems and dependencies, growth over time, long journeys and milestones
  - `micro_body`: Inside the body and the microscopic: health and hygiene, wellbeing science (stress, sleep, breathing, digestion), food safety and infection control, how learning changes the brain, biology for non-specialists
  - `nature`: Nature and sustainability: environment, carbon and energy, sustainable sourcing and supply chains in the real world, water and pollution, land use and biodiversity, outdoor safety
  - `office`: Corporate office: workplace behaviour, feedback, meetings, policy, onboarding, wellbeing, hybrid work
  - `retail`: Retail and e-commerce: customer service, complaints and refunds, payments and fraud, age-restricted sales, shoplifting and conflict, slips and spills, manual handling, deliveries and click and collect, accessibility
  - `space`: Space and cosmic scale: big-idea explainers and scale comparisons, satellites as everyday infrastructure (navigation, timing, weather, communications), teamwork and procedures in high-stakes operations, technology and future topics
  - `tech_cyber`: Technology and cyber: information security, phishing, passwords and MFA, data handling, physical security and tailgating, incident response, AI literacy, secure software practices
  - `travel`: Travel and hospitality: customer service for travel, booking and change policies, airport and hotel operations, duty of care, accessibility, fraud in bookings
  - `warehouse`: Warehouse and logistics: forklift and pedestrian safety, manual handling, picking accuracy, loading-dock safety, near-miss reporting, shift briefings and handover
